deep.reconstruction:
This page is printed in Fraktur type, not handwritten. It appears to be p. 23 (signature B4) of the school textbook that the 'HB.Leiste' bundle is built around, probably Christian Leiste's 'Die Arithmetik und Algebra' (Wolfenbüttel, 1790); that identification is my inference. Gauss's handwritten notes are on the surrounding interleaved leaves. This page itself shows no Gauss annotations.

§60 (end of the section on imaginary roots): states sqrt(-ab)/sqrt(+a) = sqrt(-b). Example: sqrt(-4)/sqrt(+2) = sqrt(-2) = sqrt(2)*sqrt(-1), citing §58. Special case a = b = 1: sqrt(-1)/sqrt(+1) = sqrt(-1) = -1/sqrt(-1), citing §57. In modern terms, i = -1/i, because i*i = -1.

§61: -sqrt(-1) = +1/sqrt(-1). Proof: -1*sqrt(-1) = (-1)*(-1)/sqrt(-1), using sqrt(-1) = -1/sqrt(-1) from §57. This equals +1/sqrt(-1) by the sign rule (-1)(-1) = +1 (§39). In modern terms, 1/i = -i.

Second Part, 'Calculation with composite numbers'.

§62: explains decimal place-value notation by powers of 10. Every integer or fraction is a sum of digits times powers of 10, with positive exponents for the integer part and negative exponents for fractions. Examples: 600 = 6*10^2 and 6/100 = 6*10^-2 (§51). If one writes only the exponent beside each digit, position becomes unnecessary. Example: 4^{+8} 3^{+6} 2^{+4} 5^{+1} 3^{0} 7^{-1} 8^{-3} 6^{-4} means 4*10^8 + 3*10^6 + 2*10^4 + 5*10 + 3 + 7/10 + 8/1000 + 6/10000. The text then explains the decimal comma (a point is also allowed) and the leading 0 for pure decimals: 0,7 = 7/10 and 0,008 = 8/1000.

§63 (begins): Problem: add or subtract integers and decimal fractions. Solution: write digits of the same power of 10 under one another (per §8.1) and carry into higher places. The text continues on the next page with borrowing.
errors: The printed result of the §62 example is written 40302053,7086 (8 integer digits). The correct value is 403020053.7086, since 400000000 + 3000000 + 20000 + 50 + 3 = 403020053. A zero is missing, almost certainly a typesetting error.
No other errors. The imaginary-unit manipulations in §§60-61 are correct for the principal values, i = -1/i and -i = 1/i. The general rule sqrt(-ab)/sqrt(a) = sqrt(-b) holds for a, b > 0.

results.what: Elementary rules for sqrt(-1): sqrt(-ab)/sqrt(a) = sqrt(-b), i = -1/i, -i = 1/i
results.modern_name: basic arithmetic of the imaginary unit

results.what: Decimal positional notation explained as a sum of digit*10^k, including negative exponents for decimal fractions
results.usually_credited_to: Indian-Arabic numeral system; decimal fractions popularized by Stevin (1585)

results.what: Column addition/subtraction of decimals with carrying

deep.surprise_reason: This is a printed page of an elementary 18th-century arithmetic textbook, not Gauss's own work. It shows no handwritten contribution by Gauss, and the content is entirely routine school material.

transcription_corrections: This page is printed text (textbook p. 23, signature B4), not Gauss's handwriting.

The result in §62 reads '40302053,7086' in the print, a single 8-digit integer part; the transcription's '403020 53,7086' inserts a spurious space. The print itself omits a zero (correct value 403020053,7086).
The image shows '2c000' (a damaged '20000'); the transcription's 20000 is the intended reading.
In §60 the second denominator is poorly printed ('√+ :'); the reading √+2 is consistent with the mathematics.
